pattern.name: Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests
pattern.summary: Counterparties' auditors need third-party valuations of their derivatives, and the Confirmations group (Larry Joe Hunter, Ellen Wallumrod) must supply them. Confirmations has no system that values deals, so each request is emailed to every Risk desk head (5 or 6 of them). Each desk head forwards it to an analyst, who pulls a mini-book for that counterparty as of a past date, exports it to Excel, blacks out sensitive columns (Delta/Vol) and replies. Confirmations then combines the desk replies. Hunter says requests come several times a week.

pattern.name: Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases

Greg Couch asked every book admin who uses WeaponX, across six managers' groups, to compact their file by hand at least once a week: open it holding the shift key, run Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database, wait for it to finish, then use it as normal. pattern.name: Monthly roll of Sitara transport usage tickets
pattern.summary: Before each new month Heidi Withers (rates group) goes through the HPL and third-party transport usage tickets in Sitara one by one, adds the new month where needed and refreshes each rate by hand to match the rate matrix. When she adds a month she leaves the volume at zero, so the schedulers on Daren Farmer's desk must fill in volumes and are told to check every pipe. The correct rates already sit in Unify for invoicing, so the Sitara tickets are a second, hand-kept copy, and mismatches with the matrix have been found.

occurrences.quote: I updated the June transport usage tickets today through HPL, and will be finishing these tickets tomorrow.
I have input and updated transport usage tickets for July.

observations.quote: Rates have been updated to reflect current matrix rates and all baseload rates that I know of at this time.
observations.note: Rates are refreshed by hand against the matrix on every ticket; the job would fill these automatically.

observations.quote: Rule of thumb was that if I had to add a month, I refreshed the rate but left volume at zero.
observations.note: Added months start at zero volume, which creates re-entry work for the schedulers.

observations.quote: I would advise that your schedulers check volumes on all pipes to ensure they're reflected in Position Manager correctly.
observations.note: The desk's schedulers are drawn into checking every pipe after the roll.

observations.quote: The tickets are finished.
observations.note: Sent the next morning: the roll ran from the afternoon of 24 May into the morning of 25 May, roughly a working day of Heidi's time.

observations.quote: The rates are in the system correctly in Unify (so that we can invoice correctly), but Daren's group uses a Sitara deal (the transport usage tickets) to estimate desk transport in the P&L during the month.
observations.note: The correct rates already exist in a system, so the Sitara rates are a duplicate copy that could be filled from it.

observations.note: Hand-kept ticket rates drift from the matrix.

pattern.name: Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing
pattern.summary: Around each NYMEX close, Stacey Vallejo (Calgary settlements) emails 5 to 8 Houston risk controllers. She asks each of them to search all their books for deals that settle between ECC and an outside counterparty and move ('flip') them to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, usually by end of day. Darron Giron forwards each request to 5 to 7 book administrators, who check their own books. EnronOnline deals land in Houston books automatically, so the mistake comes back every month. EnronOnline already books TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada deals to ECC automatically, but other parties (Duke, Aquila Canada Corp.) are not covered. Some are entered as ENA deals and slip past the search entirely. Invoicing for both ECC and ENA waits until the deals are fixed. One controller built a private calc to find the deals, and others ask to copy it.

pattern.name: Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing
pattern.summary: Each month the auditors from Arthur Andersen (Mark Austin, Sharon Smith, Carrie Richardson) email the gas Risk desk heads (Kelly, Keiser, Giron, Baumbach) a list of books. For each book they want the P&L top page for the last day of the month. If most of the P&L comes from curve shift, they also want the top pages and curve shift reports for the five largest days. Each desk head forwards the email to two to seven book admins. The admins pull the reports from ERMS and print or copy them, and the desk head passes them on to the auditors. The auditors chase missing books ('2nd request', quarter-file close-out) and ask who is responsible for each desk.

In review of our third quarter file, we have not received the P&L top pages or curve shift reports for the following regions: West Firm, FT Northwest and Mgmt. West.
We are requesting that you supply the P & L top pages for the last day of the month for those regions that are applicable to you.
Please make sure this guy gets what he needs.

pattern.name: Monthly wholesale-volume variance explanations for Investor Relations
pattern.summary: Each month Business Analysis & Reporting (Misti Day) emails about 11 commercial contacts to open the "Statistical Database", review their region's wholesale volumes for the month, and email back a verification plus a written explanation for every change of 10% or more year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month, by a deadline a few days later. Each person finds their flagged lines, works out the cause and types a free-text reply. BA&R then gathers the separate email replies for Investor Relations. The causes often carry over from month to month: in June and September the Texas reply gave the same reasons (more EOL trading and Entex taking more gas).

occurrences.quote: Please review the analysis for August 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances.
Please review the analysis for May 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances.

observations.quote: Please forward your verification and explanations via e-mail to me by 10:00am Friday, September 22.

observations.note: June reply for Texas.

observations.note: September reply for Texas gives the same causes as June, so last month's text would have needed only a confirmation.

pattern.name: Nightly check that every post ID is officialized
pattern.summary: Each night the gas book administrators must officialize every post ID (book) so the V@R and credit systems pick it up. Since October 2000, after a missed West-NW-GDL book put the desk on Risk's daily list of non-officialized books (sent to Sally Beck and reviewed weekly by Rick Buy), one person per desk group runs an Excel macro by hand: they enter the date and the Portfolio and Book codes, and the macro lists the books that are officialized. The groups led by Gossett, Baumbach, Kelly, Giron and Keiser each got this file, and staff pass round changed versions of it. Regional controllers also get an end-of-night sheet confirming all books are officialized, and Risk keeps its own daily list of misses. No system holds the full list of books each admin must officialize, so Darron Giron writes it out by hand when another group asks (Rahmaan in July, Connie Sutton and Susan Trevino in November 2000). The check used before the macro compared positions only, so it missed post IDs with no net position. Credit needs those flat books officialized too.

pattern.name: Monthly support for gas liquidation values
pattern.summary: After each month's liquidation flash, Jim Little emails the gas desk leads (Phillip Love, Darron Giron) asking for the deals behind each region's liquidation value, sometimes broken down by position type (price, basis, Gas Daily swaps, capacity hedges). Darron forwards the request to his analyst, Patrick Ryder, who pulls the deal detail and either saves it to the ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations folder or emails it to Jim. Requests come months after the fact (November values asked for in late February, December values in late March), and Jim has to ask again for months that were never saved.

occurrences.quote: Darron, I need support for: West 8,340,379 Denver 2,441,357
In need liquidation support for the December Liquidation values below

observations.quote: Get this to Jim.
observations.note: The desk lead passes the request to an analyst, who does the pull. That is two people besides Jim for each request.

observations.quote: I WILL ALSO NEED SUPPORT FOR THE DECEMBER AND JANUARY VALUES FOR ALL OF YOUR REGIONS IF YOU HAVEN'T ALREADY SAVE THEM OUT TO THE ABOVE DIRECTORY.
observations.note: Support is owed for every month and region, and months that were not saved have to be chased. A report saved automatically at close removes the chasing.

observations.quote: You may save the support to ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/"year"/"month"
observations.note: There is already a fixed place for the support, so a scheduled report can write there.

observations.quote: Please get this info to Jim. Thanks.
observations.note: The same forward-to-analyst chain a month later, this time for Denver's December values.

observations.quote: We are still unable to provide support out of ERMS for the liquidations relating to transport.
observations.note: Transport liquidations cannot come from ERMS, so they would still need a manual explanation. The savings count only the deal pull for the other position types.

stalls.quote: Please let me know when this may be available.
stalls.note: Jim cannot finish supporting the November flash until the desks pull the detail, three months after the month closed.

pattern.name: Nightly Path Confirmation checkouts with counterparties
pattern.summary: Each night the Portland Real Time shift phones at least 27 named marketers and utilities between HE 19 and HE 21 to check out prescheduled power paths, and records each confirmation in the Enpower Path Confirmation tool. Each confirmation opens a screen where the trader types the counterparty's contact details, and because the save writes straight to Enpower it takes about a minute. Cut paths are also recorded as path confirms, which adds more saves.

occurrences.quote: You must check out with all major marketers and utilities each night.
In the Enpower Path Confirmation, we need to make cuts as Path Confirms. Enter comments in the confirmed section.

observations.quote: Confirm a path by highlighting and clicking the telephone icon. A screen will come up requesting contact information from the appropriate counterparty. Because this information saves directly to Enpower, save time runs about a minute.
observations.note: Each confirmation means typing the contact details and then waiting about a minute for the save. The background save removes the wait, and pre-filling removes most of the typing.

observations.quote: This would include but not be limited to: AEP, AES-New Energy, Aquila, Avista, Calpine, Constellation, Coral, Duke, Dynegy, El Paso Merchant, Exelon, Meico, Mirant, Morgan, NCPA, Reliant, PPLMontana, PowerX, Sempra, SMUD, TransAlta, Williams, and southwest utilities such as Pinnacle West, SRP, PNM, PSCO and Pacificorp.
observations.note: 27 counterparties are named, and the list is a minimum. Since a counterparty's paths can be highlighted together, that means at least about 27 saves a night.

observations.quote: Sort by counterparty while making confirmation calls. When all schedules with that counterparty are confirmed, highlight each schedule
observations.note: Confirmations are done one counterparty at a time, which supports counting about one save per counterparty.

observations.quote: These checkouts should be started in HE 19 and finished by HE 21.
observations.note: All the checkouts must fit into a two-hour window, so about 27 minutes of save waits takes a large share of it.

observations.quote: You must check out with all major marketers and utilities each night.
observations.note: says how often the work is done

pattern.name: Giron's daily email sign-off on the Enovate DPR
pattern.summary: Each business day an Enovate analyst (Daniel Falcone, later Chris Abel, then Anita Luong) emails the Enovate DPR (daily profit-and-loss and position report) 'For your approval' to Richard Tomaski, Kevin Radous and Darron Giron. Giron replies by email, either with a bare 'OK' or by stating the net open position he shows, so the analyst can check it against the report. Approvals can fall behind: in February Tomaski asked whether the 13 Feb report had gone out, and Giron then approved the 13th and 14th together.

pattern.name: Real Time desk's hand-figured congestion revenue emails to Volume Management
pattern.summary: When the Portland Real Time desk is paid by the California grid operator (CAISO) for relieving transmission congestion, Bill Williams, the Real Time lead, works out the megawatts, hours, price and dollars from the inc sheet (the desk's schedule sheet) and emails them to Volume Management so the revenue gets into the daily California flash and settlement. In July and August 2001 several of these went to a 10-person list; others went to Jim Reyes and Darren Cavanaugh alone. When the revenue is missing from the flash, or when CAISO awarded wheels that never made it onto the inc sheet, he writes again to chase it.

occurrences.quote: Total volume was 96 mws at $248, revenue should be $23808.
This should equal $54059.64 in congestion revenue to ECTRT.
This should be at total revenue of $22,269.00.
Total revenue should be $52768.
We recieved congestion relief revenue from the CAISO for Sunday and Monday, August 12th and 13th.
We relieved Path 15 congestion for HE 7 on Saturday morning.
We are missing the congestion revenue from HE 7 on Saturday morning (10 mws at $99.00) in the flash we received yesterday.
We relieved congestion this morning (08/16/01). The hours and volumes are in the inc sheet.
We should receive revenue of $3891.31 from these wheels.
We also received congestion for HE 5--50 mws at $74.83. HE 5 is not in the inc sheet but will be.
Please use the inc sheet or CAPS to settle in the morning.

observations.note: Bill lists the hours and volumes and multiplies them out by hand, then sends the result to ten people.

observations.note: When revenue does not reach the flash, the trader has to notice and chase it; an automatic CAPS-to-flash comparison would flag this.

observations.quote: We had two wheels that were not in the inc sheet but were awarded by the CAISO and are in finals in CAPS.

pattern.name: Weekly check that new ERMS curves exist in RisktRAC
pattern.summary: When a trader needs a new price curve, the commodity group's risk management builds it in ERMS. They then fill in a curve set-up form so that Risk Analysis and Reporting can set it up again in RisktRAC, the system that calculates VaR. Separately, they email IT to add the curve to TAGG. Desks have not always sent the form, so Risk Analysis and Reporting now checks by hand every week that all curves newly set up in ERMS are also in RisktRAC. The first check found numerous curves missing, and each has to be resolved with the desk. Until a curve is in RisktRAC, its positions are left out of VaR, so VaR is wrong.

occurrences.quote: Risk Analysis and Reporting has implemented a new process in which on a weekly basis new curves set up in ERMS are reviewed to ensure that these have been set up in RisktRAC.

observations.quote: We did this for the first time today and noted numerous curves in ERMS that are not in RisktRAC - which we are working with you to resolve.
observations.note: The weekly check turns up many missing curves, and each one is then followed up with the desk.

observations.quote: If the curve is not set up in RisktRAC the positions are not captured in the VAR or engine, thereby making VAR inaccurate.
observations.note: Why the gap matters: a curve missing from RisktRAC leaves its positions out of VaR until someone finds it.

observations.quote: In the past few months, the procedures for setting up new curves and books have not been followed by everyone.
observations.note: The hand-completed form is not reliably sent, which is why the weekly check was started.

observations.note: The same curve is set up a second time in RisktRAC from a form that is filled in by hand.

observations.quote: I set up these new curves this morning and need them added to Tagg
observations.note: New curves are also requested separately from IT for TAGG, a third system that a nightly comparison could cover.

observations.quote: on a weekly basis new curves set up in ERMS are reviewed
observations.note: says how often the work is done

pattern.name: Nightly El Paso Electric model-vs-CARP tie-out
pattern.summary: On the Portland Real Time desk, the shift trader who markets El Paso Electric (EPE) must, when the trading day is done, tie out the El Paso model spreadsheet against the CARP report by eye, then log the El Paso totals in a separate monthly EPE reconciliation workbook and explain every variance. The sheet must be filled in even when nothing differs, because Houston takes an empty sheet to mean the CARP was not run. Traders sometimes skip it. Differences that are not caught surface at the monthly checkout with El Paso and Settlements; the June 2001 checkout took five days to sort out.

occurrences.quote: 3. El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done. Check spreadsheet formulas.
4. El Paso totals should be logged in the reconciliation model (m://electric/epe/epe01/aug01/epe reconciliation model) and all variances explained.
Even if there are no variances, please complete the July EPE Reconciliation sheet going forward.
reconciling the CARP are basic expectations for this position and MUST be met.

observations.quote: I just skimmed through the first 8 days of this month, and we show no variances between the Real Time El Paso model and our CARP report.
observations.note: Many nights have no differences at all, yet each still needs an entry typed by hand; an automatic comparison would write those entries itself.

observations.quote: Houston will assume that no one ran the CARP if the sheet has no entries.
observations.note: The entry is required as proof the check was done, even when it records nothing.

observations.quote: You will know you've done this correctly when the CARP report EXACTLY matches the El Paso model.
observations.note: The test is an exact match between two reports, which a spreadsheet can check mechanically.

observations.quote: Our checkout with Kathy and the Settlements group took approximately five minutes, as opposed to the five days we spent sorting it out last month.
observations.note: Differences that slip through the nightly check are costly at month-end; this saving is not counted in the minutes.
